open_questions: One kick pedal or a double: he played a four-piece with one bass drum (Modern Drummer 2008), but the human tab of Teenage Mustache has runs of five to sixteen kick 16ths at 165-200 and he describes his blast as '16ths on the kick drum'. A pedal-side camera would settle it.
Which cymbals when: Zildjian crashes at Hellfest 2003 (the logo is legible), Paiste per Wikipedia (undated, sourced to a 2008 gear blog that is about the bassist). Models and sizes unknown.
The 28-inch concert bass drum is his kit of 2012; which bass drum he played on Plague Soundscapes and at Hellfest 2003 is not stated.
The Trap Set podcast, episode 96 (9 November 2016), is a long interview with him: not heard for this record.
What Dave Astor's drumming on the 1994-2001 records was like, in any source: nothing beyond Bray's remark that Serbian plays blasts better.
Whether he drummed or sang in Dead Cross's first line-up (2015): the sources read say singer.

identity.name: Gabe Serbian

evidence.note: Consistent with his age as given in 2003 (26) and 2011 (33).
The band announced on 1 May 2022 that he had died the day before; NME gives 30 April and his age as 44. Wikipedia's infobox gives 29 April. No cause was given.

persona.description: Not a character: the Locust played as a unit in matching insect 'uniforms', faces hidden, credited under their own names. The four stood in a line across the front of the stage with the drums among them rather than behind, and the set list was built around his drumming.
persona.costume: In 2003 (Plague Soundscapes, Hellfest): the band's olive drab uniform, 'formfitting full-body suits colored a dingy green ... rough like unfinished canvas, but skintight like spandex', with mesh vents at the upper arms and a close hood whose 'mouths and eyes are big fishnet circles'; on him a sleeveless dark top with olive binding and a red stripe across the chest, khaki trousers and bare arms. Later suits changed colour (grey in 2004-2007, white by 2008); the last five were made by Ben Warwas.

identity.summary: The Locust's drummer from 2001 to his death in 2022, after three years as its second guitarist; before that Cattle Decapitation's first drummer and then its guitarist. Self-made at speed ('I never had a plan on how to play like I play'), he drove the San Diego band's sub-minute songs of grindcore, hardcore and synthesiser noise on a plain four-piece Ludwig: blasts, crash-and-snare runs over a running kick, tom pickups into the backbeat and stop-start stabs choked by the hand that struck them, in mixed meters, masked and in the band's insect uniform. Slayer and Dave Lombardo made him a drummer; Lombardo later named him. Also Head Wound City, Retox, Holy Molar, Le Butcherettes and Zu.

traditions.impact: 'When I was a kid and decided that I wanted to play drums it was because of the first time I ever heard Slayer ... Dave Lombardo was the reason I started playing drums.'
'Stuff like Dale Crover. Growing up those were my main influences, and various punk bands.'

traditions.tradition: School band and a jazz-drumming stepfather
traditions.impact: Drums in sixth-grade band after clarinet; his stepfather, a jazz drummer, had a kit and taught him a rock beat. Otherwise self-taught: practises only on the kit, never on pads or rudiments.

formative_events.event: Cattle Decapitation formed in San Diego with Serbian on drums and Dave Astor on bass; when Travis Ryan joined, Astor took the drums and Serbian the guitar.
Joined the Locust as its second guitarist, on the self-titled debut album, with Astor on drums.
Took the Locust's drums when Astor left for Cattle Decapitation, after Flight of the Wounded Locust; the Peel Session of that year was his first recording on them.
Toured with Fantomas, Dave Lombardo on drums, and Trevor Dunn's Trio-Convulsant with Ches Smith: the three drummers played together each night, a beat each and solos over them.

evidence.note: The year is from Wikipedia's mention of a 2005 Fantomas tour; the interview gives none.

eras.label: Guitarist (Cattle Decapitation and the Locust)
eras.context: Cattle Decapitation's first drummer, then its guitarist on Human Jerky and Homovore; the Locust's second guitarist on the 1998 album and Flight of the Wounded Locust, with Dave Astor drumming.

eras.label: The Locust's drummer
eras.context: The Peel Session (2001), Plague Soundscapes (2003), Safety Second, Body Last (2005) and New Erections (2007), all but the first with Alex Newport; touring in the uniforms with Fantomas, the Yeah Yeah Yeahs and on their own, then a hiatus.
defining_traits: blasts of 16ths on kick and snare
crash and snare together over a running kick

eras.label: Los Angeles bands, and the Locust again
eras.context: Retox, Le Butcherettes, Head Wound City, Skinwalker, Cheap Curls; the Locust back from 2013 (Desert Daze 2019, a 2021 House of Blues set) until his death.

genres.name: Grindcore / powerviolence
genres.notes: Albert Mudrian's Choosing Death files the Locust under grindcore; the band began as a powerviolence project.

genres.name: Noise rock
genres.notes: 'If noise-rock had superheroes, the Locust would surely be among them' (New York Times, 2007).

evidence.note: 'Muscling through each 16th note like he was laying down a punch'; no measurement.

dynamics.balance: Everything loud and at once: snare and crash together, kick under them, stops of dead silence between; no ghost-note texture in the tabs read.

feel_profile.interaction: Plays the riff's changes with the guitar and keyboard as written parts, not grooves: short movements stitched together, stops on cue, and on stage he cues the band ('conducts his band-mates through half-a-dozen songs, full of abrupt changes, stops, and signaling').

hand_techniques.name: Crash and snare together
hand_techniques.description: The right hand on a crash and the left on the snare in unison on the beats or the off-beats, over a kick in 16ths (Teenage Mustache at 200), or a crash on every beat with the backbeat under it.

hand_techniques.name: Tom pickups into the backbeat
hand_techniques.description: Two or three 16ths on the rack tom just before the snare on 2 or 4, or a run of six to the bar line, under a crash on the beats.

hand_techniques.name: Choked cymbal stabs
hand_techniques.description: A crash struck with the kick and caught at once by the same hand, then silence: the stop-start hits of AOTKPTA and of the band's changes ('jaunty punch-pause').

hand_techniques.name: Rolls round the toms
hand_techniques.description: Single-stroke runs across the big rack tom at his left and the floor tom at his right, a long reach on his layout.

hand_techniques.name: Snare ruffs
hand_techniques.description: Three fast strokes into the next beat in the 3/4 bars of The Half-Eaten Sausage.

foot_techniques.name: Running kick under the hands
foot_techniques.description: Bursts of five 16ths (Teenage Mustache's verse) or a bar of continuous 16ths under crash and snare; on one bass drum in his four-piece, how many pedals is not settled.

devices_search.note: None found. The Half-Eaten Sausage moves from 4/4 to a run of 3/4 bars and the machine tabs change meter and tempo almost every bar: mixed meter, not a device. Teenage Mustache's five-16th kick runs resolve inside the bar. One machine-tab bar of Twenty-Three Lubed Up puts crash and kick every three 16ths across a 4/4 bar (a 3-against-4 grouping) but it is a single bar of a machine transcription and no human source repeats it, so it is not taken.

voice_language.hihat: Little hi-hat: an open hat on the beats in the slower 3/4 bars; the right hand lives on the crashes and the ride.
voice_language.snare: Backbeat on 2 and 4 at punk tempos, 16ths in the blasts, in unison with the crash on the beats and off-beats, pairs of 16ths after the crash, ruffs.
voice_language.kick: Under the crash on the beats, in bursts of 16ths, continuous 16ths in the blasts.
voice_language.toms: Pickups of two or three 16ths into the backbeat and runs to the bar line on the big rack tom; rolls across rack and floor.
voice_language.cymbals: Crashes on every beat or every half bar, choked for stops; the ride in the centre of the kit, both crashes low and close.

implements.notes: Pro-Mark Japanese oak, 2B for years, then 5B.

aesthetic: a big, live four-piece hit hard
snare and crash together at the front
dry, close, compressed in a crowded mix of synthesisers and screaming

by_era.description: Alex Newport's productions (Plague Soundscapes, Safety Second, Body Last, New Erections): tight, loud, little room, the kit as a percussive part of the riff under keyboards.

sample_hints.2003: Big Ludwig shells hit hard: a deep, damped kick, a cracking metal snare, low-tuned toms, washy crashes choked short.

evidence.note: The producer and the kit are sourced; the sound is described from them, not from a review.

signature_traits.label: Crash and snare together over a running kick
signature_traits.description: Teenage Mustache's fastest bars: crash and snare in unison on the beats and the off-beats, the kick in continuous 16ths under them.

signature_traits.label: Blasts: 16ths on kick and snare
signature_traits.description: 'It's pretty much playing as fast as you can play on everything at once ... I'm doing 16ths on the kick drum and on the snare drum, and that varies with what I'm doing with my right hand and the cymbal.' His guitarist: 'how much better Gabe plays blast beats than our old drummer Dave'.

signature_traits.label: Stop-start stabs
signature_traits.description: Bursts of a few seconds cut off dead ('the drums were like lines of dialogue, clearly delineated bursts five seconds long'), crash and kick on a cue and the crash choked at once; on stage he cues the changes.

signature_traits.label: Songs as written movements
signature_traits.description: Parts written, not jammed: 'We'll work out different movements and then we'll figure out how to tie them together', each sub-minute song taking a long time; he writes fast parts at speed, and the drums sometimes change the riff.

signature_traits.label: A four-piece laid out wide
signature_traits.description: A plain four-piece Ludwig with the big rack tom far to his left, the ride in the middle where a rack tom would be, toms and ride low and flat, the crashes low and close.

signature_traits.label: Masked, in the band's insect uniform
signature_traits.description: Played in a close hood with mesh eyes and mouth and the band's body suit, in a line with the others at the front of the stage; at a hot show he would strip the top and lift the hood off his mouth.

evidence.note: 'Dave Lombardo was the reason I started playing drums.' Lombardo in turn named him: 'Their drummer is named Gabe Serbian, and their music hits me now like D.R.I. hit me in the early '80s.'
Nightly three-drummer jams on the Fantomas tour; later Dead Cross with Lombardo and Pearson.

Astor drummed for the Locust 1994-2001: the splits with Man Is the Bastard (1995) and Jenny Piccolo (1996), the 1997 EP, The Locust (1998), the Arab on Radar split (2000) and Flight of the Wounded Locust (2001). He left for Cattle Decapitation, where in 1997 he had taken the drums from Serbian, and later founded Pathology.
In both bands at once: Astor on drums and Serbian on guitar in the Locust (1998-2001) and in Cattle Decapitation (1997-2001).
The nightly three-drummer jams with Lombardo on the Fantomas tour.
400 Blows' drummer: 'Some of the best drumming I have seen in a long time.'
The Locust, Retox, Head Wound City, Dead Cross. 'I like to think he and I had shared telepathy through music.'
Also Skinwalker.

philosophy.idea: Play a lot, on the kit: if you just play every day your chops stay up and you can go fast when you need to; pads and rudiments in front of the television he gave up.
Write fast parts fast: slower parts are easier to write at a faster tempo.
A style is not planned; it comes naturally and evolves, rather than sitting down to work out something never played before.

innovations: Grindcore and hardcore speed played as written, stop-start movements under synthesisers
The drummer in line with the band at the front of the stage, masked, cueing the changes

cultural_references.description: Dave Lombardo, his first idol, compared the Locust's effect on him to D.R.I.'s in the early 1980s and named its drummer.
After his death in 2022 the Locust said it could no longer be active; its last recording is a remix of Danny Elfman's 'Cruel Compensation'.

common_misconceptions: That he drummed on the early Locust records: Dave Astor did, to 2001; Serbian played guitar on them.

generation_rules: Straight 16ths, no swing, no ghost notes; everything loud.
Crash on the beats or on 1 and 3, snare with it or just after, the kick running 16ths under it.
Blasts of 16ths on kick and snare under a crash on the beats.
Punk backbeat at 165-190 with two or three tom 16ths into each snare.
Short sections that change abruptly, stops of dead silence, crash-and-kick stabs choked at once.
Mixed meter: 4/4 sections broken by runs of 3/4 bars.
Fills short: tom pickups, a run of six to the bar line, a snare ruff.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Slayer made him a drummer; he played the Locust's grind as written movements, masked, from 2001 to 2022, taking the chair from Dave Astor.
